post.description:
Authenticate a user and return JWT tokens.

Security notes:
  - Same error message for wrong email AND wrong password
    (prevents user enumeration attacks)
  - Timing: bcrypt.verify is slow by design — prevents brute force

Exchange a valid refresh token for a new access token.

Why not just extend the access token's lifetime?
  - Short-lived access tokens limit damage if one is stolen
  - Refresh tokens can be revoked (stored in Redis blacklist)

Revoke the current access token by adding its JTI to the Redis blacklist.

The token remains cryptographically valid but will be rejected on next use.
Redis TTL = token's remaining lifetime → no manual cleanup needed.

get.description:
Paginated list of pseudonymized patient records.

Each row joins the patient row with last/next appointment timestamps so the
web roster can render a usable table without an N+1 round-trip.

patch.description: Patients update their own RGPD consent flags from the mobile app. Patient UUID is derived from the JWT — no path parameter needed. Uses the same audit trail logic as the doctor-managed endpoint.

Update one or more RGPD consent flags for a patient. Core consent changes (iot/nlp/sharing) are logged to immutable consent_logs; sms_opt_out preference remains audit-tracked via audit_logs. RGPD Art. 7 — consent must be specific, informed, and revocable.

get.description: Export all pseudonymized data held about a patient in machine-readable JSON. Includes: consent state, demographics, consent change history, and access log. Civil identity (name, phone) is NOT included — requires DPO-level decryption (Sprint 5). Admin-only: exporting another person's data is a sensitive operation.

delete.description: Erase a patient's personal data. Two-step operation: (1) delete civil identity from secure schema, (2) anonymize pseudonymized record in public schema. The patient UUID is preserved for audit trail integrity. Admin-only — irreversible operation.

get.description: Return the complete audit trail with optional filters. Used by the DPO to verify compliance and investigate incidents. Results are sorted newest-first. Max page size: 200 rows.

post.description: Runs a query through both Qdrant RRF (hybrid search) and the mmarco multilingual cross-encoder, then compares the rankings. Used to validate that RRF quality is sufficient for the chat hot path.

Send a message to the MediSense chatbot. Returns a complete JSON response.

- If `conversation_id` is provided, continues an existing conversation.
- Otherwise, creates a new conversation.
- For token-by-token streaming use `POST /chat/stream` instead.

schema.title: Response List Conversations Api V1 Chat Get

post.description:
Send a message and receive the response as Server-Sent Events (SSE).

The response is a unidirectional server→client stream. The client sends
one POST request; the server streams tokens as they are generated by
Mistral 7B. Time-to-first-token is typically < 200ms.

Event types:
- `lang`    — detected language ("fr" | "ar" | "darija")
- `sources` — list of retrieved chunks used as context
- `token`   — one text token from the LLM
- `done`    — final event with confidence score and conversation_id

200.description: Server-Sent Events stream. Each event is a JSON object.

delete.description:
Delete a conversation and all its messages.

RGPD Article 17 — Right to erasure: patients can delete their chat history.
CASCADE delete removes all messages automatically.

get.summary: Build AI-assisted DPA summary for a patient (doctor only)
get.description:
Build and return a DPA (Decision-support Panel) summary.

Aggregates:
  - Patient symptoms from chat history (last 7 days)
  - Biometric anomalies from IoT sensors (last 30 days)
  - Rule-based recommended actions

Creates a new dpa_summaries row in status=PENDING for doctor review.

Performance target: < 500ms P95 (symptoms + IoT fetched in parallel).

post.summary: Doctor approves AI-generated DPA summary (with optional edits)
post.description:
Doctor approves the DPA summary.

If body.edited_actions is provided → status becomes MODIFIED.
Otherwise → status becomes APPROVED.

Uses optimistic locking (version field) to prevent concurrent approvals.
Returns HTTP 409 if another doctor approved first.

post.summary: Doctor rejects AI-generated DPA summary with mandatory reason
post.description:
Doctor rejects the DPA summary.

A reason is mandatory (min 10 chars) — logged for model retraining.
Uses optimistic locking — returns HTTP 409 if already processed.

patch.summary: Doctor approves, rejects, or modifies a single recommended action
patch.description:
Doctor decides on a single action within a DPA summary.

This allows granular control: approve prescription, reject referral, etc.
The parent summary status stays PENDING until the doctor explicitly calls
/approve or /reject on the whole summary.

post.description:
POST /api/v1/appointments — patient-facing booking.

Rules:
  - patient role can only book for themselves (patient_uuid == self)
  - doctor/secretary/admin can book for any patient
  - scheduled_at must be in the future (UTC)
  - doctor_uuid must point to an active user with role=doctor
  - patient_uuid must point to an active patient
  - 409 if the doctor already has an appointment at the exact scheduled_at

ConsentUpdate.description:
Request body for PATCH /patients/{patient_uuid}/consent.

Only the fields provided are updated — fields set to None are ignored.

ErasureResponse.title: ErasureResponse
ErasureResponse.description:
Response for DELETE /patients/{patient_uuid} (US-08).

RGPD Art. 17 — Right to erasure ("right to be forgotten").

What happens on erasure:
  1. public.patients: is_active=False, ML fields anonymized (birth_year,
     sex, city_code, chronic_conditions cleared), consent flags reset
  2. secure.patients_identity: row deleted (civil identity removed)
  3. public.audit_logs: erasure event recorded (the log itself is kept
     for legal accountability — RGPD allows keeping audit trails)

The patient_uuid record is kept in public.patients (is_active=False)
to maintain referential integrity with existing appointment/audit records.

PatientDataExport.title: PatientDataExport
PatientDataExport.description:
Response for GET /patients/{patient_uuid}/data/export (US-07).

RGPD Art. 20 — Right to data portability.
Admin-only endpoint: formal data export requests are handled by the DPO,
not by individual doctors. Returns a machine-readable export of all
pseudonymized data held about the patient.

NOTE: Civil identity (name, phone, email) is NOT included here.
That data lives in secure.patients_identity and requires DPO-level
decryption (handled in a separate Sprint 5 DPO endpoint).
